newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht steadies, eyes rescue package.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht steadies, eyes rescue package.

text.p: Most Asian currencies kicked off the week on a quiet note on Monday, lulled by the holiday in Hong Kong ahead of its handover back to China at midnight after 156 years of British colonial rule, dealers said.
"The market is watching the handover. We don't expect anything to happen that will affect the markets but it is a major market and a historic event," said a dealer with a European bank.
The Hong Kong market will be closed for most of the week.
In Thailand, all eyes remained fixed on the Bank of Thailand and its rescue efforts to resuscitate the ailing financial sector.
"The whole market is riddled with rumours and people are extremely cautious. They want details of exactly what the central bank is going to do to help," said another dealer.
At 0400 GMT, spot baht was trading at 25.870/910.

Dealers said sentiment on the baht was underpinned by the central bank's moves to bolster the depressed finance sector, including forcing 16 ailing finance firms to submit merger plans in the next couple of weeks.
Further south, the Malaysian ringgit continued to be sold by big offshore players amid fears of fresh intervention by Bank Negara Malaysia around 2.5250 a dollar, dealers said.

"Dollar rinngit saw a quiet range of 2.5230/45 bids today. People are afraid of the next move by Bank Negara and watching if it is ready to sell dollar/ringgit," a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore said.

He felt that if the ringgit broke 2.5250/55 to the dollar, it could test 2.5275/325, a level which could see some resistance by the central bank looking to quell any challenge to the Malaysian curreny.
Dealers said there was no evidence of the central bank's presence in the open market on Monday morning.
They said Bank Negara intervened on Friday to sell around $100 million to support the ringgit at 2.5250 a dollar after a heavy attack on the local currency.
"The market looks poised to test 2.5250 again," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5237/47 to a dollar.
The Indonesian rupiah eased against the dollar on ample liquidity.
One foreign bank dealer said trading was slow due to a lack of fresh market factors.
"The local currency is likely to remain moving in a tight range the rest of the day due to a lack of fresh market factors," another bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was at 2,431.30/31.80 at 0320 GMT against an opening of 2,430.50/31.50.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,431.00/31.70 and 2,431.00/31.50, respectively.
Dealers said the spot rupiah rate was likely to range between 2,431.00 to 2,432.00 for the rest of the day.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia, kept its intervention band at 2,425/2,617 and its conversion band at 2,425/2,473 on Friday.
The Singapore dollar kept a tight trading range amid a lack of fresh factors. At midday, it was at 1.4294/04 to the dollar.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Angela Tan in Singapore (65-8703083)
